input.quote: The parties agree that all drawings, documents, designs, models, inventions, computer programs, computer systems, data, computer documentation and other tangible materials authored or prepared by Contractor for Company as the work product required by a Statement of Work (collectively, the "Works"), are the property of Company
input.rationale: Direction is correct: Company owns the Works (subject to payment), Contractor keeps only its pre-existing materials, and Section 4(c) grants Company a perpetual, royalty-free, sublicensable licence to any Contractor Information embedded in the Works; Works in progress are assigned to Company on termination. No assignment of Company IP or data to Contractor and no joint ownership. We note the absence of an express Customer Data ownership statement, which we raise as a comment rather than a deviation; the licence-scope gaps are addressed under LICENSE.

input.quote: Contractor hereby grants to Company a royalty-free, non- exclusive perpetual license (including the right to grant a sublicense) to use, copy, modify, create, derivative version, publicly perform and publicly display such Contractor's Information in connection with Company's business operations.
input.rationale: The grant is perpetual and sublicensable, but it does not name Company's affiliates or contractors, is not stated to be irrevocable, and is not transferable to a successor (compounded by the consent-based assignment bar in §10), so it misses the fallback (affiliates covered; transferable in an M&A transaction). Section 4(b) also restricts Company's use of Contractor property to "the software Company receives under this Agreement". Redline adds affiliates/contractors, "irrevocable" and successor transferability with minimal edits.
